description: Establish the feature branch and a green offline baseline so later changes are measured against a known-good state. Create ONE feature branch off main (do NOT push). Confirm the offline gates that CAN run in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox pass on the untouched tree: per-crate `cargo fmt --check` for the crates this task will touch, and (from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend) the whole-directory `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .`. Record which gates are runnable offline vs. CI-only so the implementation features know their self-audit surface.
steps: From /projects/agent-harbor (clean main at v0.9.0) create and check out ONE feature branch, e.g. `git checkout -b feat/real-auto-routing`. Do NOT push, tag, or open a PR.

From hybrid-orchestrator/ run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check`, and the same for crates/routing, crates/orchestrator-core, crates/tauri-app, crates/persistence. Confirm all clean (they should be on untouched main). Record the exact commands.

Attempt `cargo build --manifest-path crates/routing/Cargo.toml` and `cargo test --manifest-path crates/routing/Cargo.toml` (routing's unit tests need no network and its deps are lighter). Record whether they compile/pass in-sandbox; if the crates.io fetch 403s, note that this crate too is CI-gated.

Attempt the same build/test for crates/providers to learn whether it compiles in-sandbox (it may fail on rustc 1.92 vs AWS-SDK deps). Record the outcome so FEAT-002 knows whether it can rely on local cargo or must hand-audit.

From hybrid-orchestrator/frontend run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` and record that it passes on the untouched tree. Check whether node_modules exists (so `npm run test`/`npm run lint`/`npm run build` are runnable offline) and record it.
Write the runnable-vs-CI-only findings into this feature's `findings` field so FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 know exactly what they can verify locally.
acceptance_criteria: A single new feature branch exists off main and is checked out; nothing is pushed.
`cargo fmt --check` passes for providers, routing, orchestrator-core, tauri-app, persistence on the untouched tree.
`NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` passes from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend on the untouched tree.
findings records which of {cargo build/test per crate, npm test/lint/build, prettier} are runnable offline vs. CI-only.
verification: Run `git branch --show-current` and confirm it is the new feature branch (not main).
Re-run the per-crate `cargo fmt --check` commands and the whole-frontend `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` and confirm exit 0.
findings:
Branch: created and checked out `feat/real-auto-routing` off clean main at v0.9.0 (commit a319603). Nothing pushed/tagged; no PR.

OFFLINE GATES CONFIRMED GREEN ON UNTOUCHED TREE:
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml --check` (run from hybrid-orchestrator/) is CLEAN for ALL five target crates: providers, routing, orchestrator-core, tauri-app, persistence. This is the primary Rust offline gate FEAT-002/003 must keep green (cargo fmt does not need network or full compile).
- `NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .` (prettier 3.9.6) from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend: CLEAN ('All matched files use Prettier code style!'). This is the primary frontend offline gate.

RUNNABLE OFFLINE vs CI-ONLY:
- RUNNABLE OFFLINE: (1) per-crate `cargo fmt --check` for all touched crates; (2) whole-frontend `prettier --check .`. These two are the ONLY gates that run in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox.
- CI-ONLY (cannot run in sandbox): cargo build / cargo test / clippy for EVERY crate, INCLUDING routing. Reason: `cargo build`/`cargo test --manifest-path crates/routing/Cargo.toml` AND `crates/providers/Cargo.toml` both FAIL with `rustc 1.92.0 is not supported` — AWS-SDK transitive deps (aws-credential-types 1.3.0, aws-sigv4 1.5.1, aws-smithy-async/http/runtime-api/types, etc.) require rustc >=1.94.1. So routing is NOT independently compilable in-sandbox despite the plan's earlier assumption (it transitively pulls the AWS SDK via the workspace dep graph). crates.io fetch itself partially worked (some crates downloaded before the rustc gate error), but the compile is blocked by the toolchain version, not only the network. NOTE: bare `cargo build`/`cargo test` build nothing (workspace members array empty; all crates excluded) — must use --manifest-path.
- CI-ONLY (frontend): `npm run test` (vitest), `npm run lint` (eslint), `npm run build` (tsc+vite) are NOT runnable offline — node_modules is ABSENT in hybrid-orchestrator/frontend and npm registry is 403 under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, so `npm install` cannot populate it. A global node (v22.23.2 via nvm at /opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin, plus v18/v20/v24) and global prettier 3.9.6 ARE available, but no project deps/tsc/vitest/eslint.

IMPLICATIONS FOR FEAT-002/003 SELF-AUDIT:
- Rust: rely on `cargo fmt --check` locally; for build/test/clippy correctness, HAND-AUDIT exhaustively. In particular, any new field on AvailableModel (crates/providers/src/builtins.rs) must be updated at EVERY construction site: the list_available_models_with_build_errors loop plus test sites across routing (policies/registry.rs, manual_override.rs, tests/demo_policy_extension.rs), orchestrator-core (tests/pipeline_e2e.rs), providers (tests/demo_provider_extension.rs, tests/net_peer.rs), and tauri-app. CI (ubuntu+windows, rustc >=1.94) is the authoritative compile/test gate.
- Frontend: cannot run vitest/eslint/tsc offline. Keep TS types (frontend/src/types/index.ts) and EVERY vitest mock/fixture (invoke mocks for all Tauri commands) in sync BY HAND. Run `NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .` before finishing (prettier IS available and prettier misses have previously cost 2 CI rounds) — use node path /opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin on PATH; the `npx` shim is NOT on the default PATH, invoke the `prettier` binary directly.

No source changes made in this feature.
